verdict.rationale: Notion's own docs describe Notion MCP as the way for MCP clients such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex to connect to a workspace. The docs cover tool capabilities (search, read, create, update), OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for client connection, admin controls in Settings → Connections, security guidance, and an open-source self-hostable notion-mcp-server. A probe confirms the official MCP docs page exists. missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of connecting an agent via Notion MCP.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: Notion MCP lets an MCP client, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, connect to your Notion workspace through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Read, create, and update Notion content.
Build an MCP client that connects to Notion MCP using OAuth 2.0 with PKCE.
the notion-mcp-server package is available as an open-source implementation
Workspace owners can manage MCP client access in Settings → Connections.
official MCP server documented at https://developers.notion.com/docs/mcp
